t: Great retractable tip design and grip, but a little too heavy for fast writing
x:
I love the retractable tip and the grip. I wish every pencil could have these features, but I don't really like the weight of the pencil. It's well balanced, but it's just a bit too heavy for my tastes. I also use my papermate clearpoint, and with the jumbo twisty eraser removed or cut in half, the light weight pencil makes a great tool for scribbling down notes or an essay (although you should normally use a pen for that, I guess?) that being said, the weight is well balanced, so it feels better than my pilot p-500 with the cap on - I usually prefer to leave the cap off that pen if I'm writing something, even if it means risking losing the cap. I would also be worried if I accidentally dropped the pencil with the tip extended, not just because of the high weight, but also because the tip doesn't look like it has any elastic deformation zones or anything to soften a hit to the ground, unlike my pilot p-500 and precise v5 pens. I also don't like how if you unscrew the tip, you see a lot of plastic threads, which might not last forever, unlike aluminum. It's even more annoying how the aluminum barrel where the clip is looks super overbuilt with thick metal walls, which greatly add to the weight while they used plastic for the lower half. Also, perhaps more importantly, the 0.3mm leads frequently break inside of the pencil if I'm playing with the retractable tip a lot for some reason. The leads that came with the pencil must have been 4B or something, but even after using pentel AIN leads, I'm still losing more lead to lead breakages than actual writing. Pentel really needs to fix this, as 0.3mm lead can be expensive and hard to find.

If pentel offered replacement tips, fixed the lead breakages, made it all metal unless where necessary, and greatly reduced the weight by using thinner wall diameters (the aluminum barrel near the tip looks like it could survive getting run over by a tank, while the lower half looks like I could break it with my bare hands), that would make this into the perfect writing instrument.

t: promising design but fragile and lead jams frequently
x:
I like design, especially retractable point and the fine precise line well supported by sleeve so that it doesn't wobble.

However TWO FLAWS preventing me from giving it as a gift or recommending it wholeheartedly to others.

(1) It is FRAGILE: outside is metal but inside is brittle plastic, including the threads that hold it together.
DON'T put it in your pocket, purse, shoulder bag or brief. The pressure of items moving around can cause the plastic inner to snap - happened to us twice (2 out of the three pens we purchased for office and home use snapped in the first 30 days!).

(2) The frequently jams as it reaches the final 1/2 inch of the lead. By frequently, I mean at least once in every 5 leads. This has occurred with all three pencils we purchased. And once jammed, it is VERY DIFFICULT remove the jammed lead. It requires a wire or needs that is less than .3mm in diameter - this tool is not supplied by Pentel. You can use one strand of a breaded speaker wire.

I will continue to use it - but will handle it very carefully & transport it in a hard shell pencil case or eyeglass case (needs to be 7" long) Despite these two limits, when it works it performs better than any other .3mm mechanical pencil we have tested.

t: My Favorite Go-To Mechanical Pencils for Many Years
x:
I enjoy sketching and painting, and I'm always on the lookout for new tools to help me work. As of late I’ve been going back through some of my art supply purchased over the years and reviewing the ones that stood out in order to hopefully help other artists make informed purchases.

I purchased my first Pentel Graph Gear 1000 mechanical pencil a little over five years ago, and have added many more to my collection in the years since. It's my go-to mechanical pencil for a number of reasons:

- It has a comfortable, chiseled metallic grip inlaid with soft latex-free pads provides writing comfort. These pads are different colors depending on the lead size you choose (brown for .3 mm, grey for .5 mm, blue for .7 mm, and yellow for .9 mm), making it easy to identify which size of lead you're using.
- The dual-action retractor advances and retracts tip for easy use. This means that you're able to retract the tip when you're storing it, which helps prevent damage to the tip as well as accidental damage (read: holes) in whatever you're storing it in.
- The lead and eraser are refillable.
- The barrel has a rotating window that allows you to identify the type of lead you've placed in it (2B, HB, etc.), so if you have multiples of these pencils, it's easy at a glance to identify what type of lead is in each without having to test them. Between this and the color-coding for the lead type, it makes it incredibly easy to keep on creating rather than having to take breaks to remember where you put a certain lead size or hardness or softness of lead. It also means that if you have multiples, you can have a variety of them handy, rather than having to regularly swap out lead.
- They are extremely well weighted.
- I rarely experience breakage.

I regularly carry the following Pentel Graph Gear 1000s in my mobile sketch kit:
- A .5 mm with 2H lead
- A .5 mm with HB lead
- A .5 mm with 2B lead
- A .3 mm with 2H lead

That said, these are by far my favorite mechanical pencils, and they are something I regularly use at home and while on the go. I would highly recommend them to any artist or draftsmen who is interested in adding a solid and long-lasting mechanical pencil to their creative arsenal.

As an engineering student four semesters in, pens have not been an option and the old, cheap, plastic BIC mechanical pencils I used to use through high school and my first three semesters at uni didn't feel right anymore. I checked out a few pencils and finally bought this one a little trepidatiously because of the price tag (I used to buy 24 pencils for less than this single one cost, after all).
I've come to love it. It writes quite smoothly and the pencil is well-balanced in your hand. The silver/blue color mix along with the metal structure gives the pencil a refined look (if you're not a student, this pencil looks business-like and can pass as a pen at a quick glance).The grip is fine with the raised metal/soft rubber(?) contrast and I have no complaints there. The grip and the tip can both be unscrewed. I took a look once then screwed it back on tightly and both parts are in no danger of coming off loose.

With my old plastic pencils, I had a (admittedly disgusting) habit of putting the clip in my mouth after which the clip would unsurprisingly break. I still do this with the Graph Gear but the clip is fine and doesn't have teeth marks (whew). I don't use the clip much in school but it has become a habit to click the top of the pencil (to push lead) and then retract with the clip. It sounds like a pen clicking, so if you're a student who can't feed your pen-clicking habit because you don't use pens anymore, you're in luck.

The eraser, which is hidden underneath a cap, is skinny and useful for erasing just the one number you mis-wrote in your equation without erasing the other numbers right next to it. It erases cleanly and with little required force, but, since it is skinny, you can erase it away within a month or two. (there are refills, available on Amazon). I'd suggest using a standalone eraser for normal erasing and using this attached eraser when you need to get in those tight spots (e.g. erase a single digit in a longer number). This is probably a good idea for students because taking the cap off every time you want to use the eraser can be slightly frustrating on a university desk, because the cap will roll off if left on it's side (though you can set it down standing vertically so it won't roll). The entire pencil is very durable, though, and no part of it, including the fragile-looking tip and cap, has been damaged after a few drops.

It was worth the >$10, coming from a university student. I hope to use this same pencil throughout my entire college career, along with the Pentel lead and erasers. This is another excellent item from Pentel.

First thoughts:

*It's a bit heavier than standard pencils, not being made of lightweight plastic. The eraser is capped (not twistable), but since I don't use pencil erasers - preferring the white erasers when needed - that wasn't an issue.

*Finally! A .5 that is actually .5!! And doesn't break! I used this pencil for three weeks straight without a single break, unlike my previous mechanical pencil that would break at least once a week; once a day if I was really busy. .3 pencils are usually too fragile for regular use but I love me a fine point - this Pentel was able to give me a fine point without the breakage.

*The clicker takes some getting used to. Most mechanical pencils require pushing down on the top and pressing the tip simultaneously to retract the lead. With this pencil, you push in the top of the clicker handle (I'm sure there's a better name for it) and everything retracts - lead, point, everything.

*Did I mention it's heavier? Not "ooh, I'm carrying a marker" heavy but... heavier than plastic pencil.

*Apparently, you can change lead styles. I accidentally switched from 2H to 2B, and thought it was broken. Experiment with each style (you just hold the bottom and twist the top barrel, watching the indicator above the grip section) to see which works for you. So far, 2H has been my best setting.

*HIDE IT. (But remember where you hid it.) At this price - and quality - you don't want your officemates "borrowing" your new favorite pencil.

I have been a fan of Pentel for over four years now. My erasers, lead, pencils, and other various office supplies have all come from you guys since. I am a student, and use all of these products on the daily. I have always been happy with their performances.
I received my first Graph Gear 1000 as a gift around Christmas of 2014, and it lasted me for several years. I loved the weight, the build, and the quality of the utensil immediately. Since, I have gifted it myself to others at least twice, and I have heard nothing but good things. In September of 2016, my pencil finally gave out, and I ordered a new one immediately. I was surprised, but not completely taken aback when my first pencil broke, as it had been several years. But my latest Graph Gear broke in the exact same way.
The plastic lip that separates the two metal halves of the utensil and holds them together cracked for no apparent reason for the SECOND TIME today. I first realized when I simply picked it up from off of my desk and noticed that the two halves were not even. When I determined that it was cracked, I recognized it from my first pencil and resigned myself to the fact that I would have to buy yet another one.

I was going to just come home and buy yet another one, but I don't seem to be at any fault here; these pencils are expensive, and I am a very loyal customer. I am happy to purchase and pay for your products as I use them, but factors out of my control should not result in me needing to spend another ten bucks, especially if it's just going to break again.
I would be happy to change my rating: as I said, I love Pentel products. But if you wouldn't mind, I would also be happy to receive a replacement pencil. Please consider both looking into this problem and sending me another pencil. If I continue to be disappointed, I will probably move on to Pilot or Bic products instead.
Once again, I love your products and want to continue to purchase and use them, but until this problem is solved, I doubt I will.

The product photo suggested that it might be a bit clunky - overkill for the purpose.  But of a half dozen of my mechanical pencils, this is the one I seem to pick up for immediate use.  I've grown to like the snap clip, which retracts and protects the writing end of the pencil.  I'm sure I'll be getting more of these for gifts.

It's an all around solid pencil.  I've had it for couple months now using it mostly for work as a regular pencil writing notes in a notebook.  This pencil performs where prior pencils I've had issues with.  For instance, the pencil lead doesn't push up when the lead gets too small.  The grip doesn't come off peel off.  The weight doesn't feel too heavy in the hands.  It's metal so the tube doesn't crack.  The pencil tip where the lead comes out retracts into the pencil so the tip or the lead doesn't break.  All around, I'm pretty pleased.

Most drafting pencils have a thin, short metal rod stuck into the eraser under the push button to clean out jams. This product lacks one meaning it is impossible to clear some jams that can occur. I used this pencil for a week before it jammed and was permanently broken. Piece of garbage.

t: Has changed my mind on mechanical pencils
x: I have always hated mechanic pencils. I would periodically try to use them, as being able to mark through small openings for woodwork and such seemed desirable--but the tips would immediately break for me. This pencil works for me! The metal reinforcement around the tip prevents the lead from snapping. It advances well, and the clip also retracts the lead entirely, so the lead won't snap in a pencil cup. I am very happy to have found this product and the fine line it draws has indeed already proved helpful on projects.

I don’t even know where to begin with this Pencil. I have had this pencil for several years and it has become my exclusive “daily driver”. Being in a rigorous engineering program in college, I do my fair share of homework, take notes, work examples, sit through multiple hour exams and anything else that you could think of. This pencil has been through it all with me; I’ve had relationships that have lasted less than this pencil. The quality of the pencil if superb, from the stainless steel barrel to the intricate retracting mechanism. The jacket for the lead has a very high tolerance and fits snugly. I rarely have any lead break on me when writing, a problem common in many cheaper pencils.
The weight is very substantial and feels good in the hand. It can be a bit awkward at first, but just feels “right” later on. I have had many friends pick it up and are surprised as to how I can use such a “heavy” pencil. The knurling on the grip is also pretty comfortable, although it will cause you to build up a callous due to the constant rubbing; this could be a problem for some. My favorite aspect is the retractable tip, as it allows for easy transport and protection. I have other metal pencils that do not have this feature, and they are always getting got in my pocket or backpack when trying to pull them out. It is also fun to just click during class, although be expecting a few annoyed glances.
This is the best pencil that I have used and have no problem recommending it to my friends, I even purchased one as a gift for a family member who was heading off to college to start his engineering program. Now if only they made it in black…

I have tried and used many mechanical pencils over the years.  Some were sort of O.K., most were not.  But this Pentel GraphGear 1000 is...AWESOME.  The feel, the comfort and sturdiness, no weak breakage of the lead, I absolutely love this pencil!  Sounds weird that a man loves his pencil, I know, but when you need to use one?  Well, you'll understand.
I hated it the slightest touch to paper the lead breaks 😒

I needed a way to write notes in books in very small letters and this pencil makes it possible.

The real perk about this pencil vs. Others is that the tip is retractable! If it falls it wont break like other pencils

t: the best mechanical pencil I have ever used
x:
My first one has been serving me for almost three years of intense use and several more years of light use, surviving numerous falls. The lead has been broken off at the tip countless times and the mechanism still functions excellently. The attached picture is the wear after all that time, notice that the core mechanisms are still in excellent condition.
I recently got another one and it seems to have all the same mechanical quality.

Pros:
- Reliable lead mechanism, always works, no fiddling
- Point retracting mechanism is strong, spring doesn't get old and weak
- No need to push on the lead to retract the tip (do not overestimate how frustrating pushing can be)
- Plastic underneath the pocket-clip is durable and shows no wear degradation
- Can actually be clipped onto pockets without risking breaking anything off
- Great feeling metal, nice weight, not flimsy.

Cons:
- Eraser under the metal cap can be a bit tricky to use, I just use an external eraser.
- Rotating lead-hardness indicator window a bit wonky to get set right, I never bother.

All in all, the price and, great construction, and reliable operation are what I like about this.
I love this pencil. The thing I like most about it is how the lead rarely breaks. When you use those cheap-o pencils, the lead breaks all the time.

t: Retractable sleeve holds lead nice and tight with virtually no breakage
x: Bought all four sizes. Been using them a while. They are built really well throughout. Very well designed and thought through. Retractable sleeve holds lead nice and tight with virtually no breakage. Grip is super comfortable. For the price, you get a lot of pencil.

t: I really want to love this pencil
x:
I really want to love this pencil..but my second one has broken again due to some inner-mechanical issue.
After my first one broke, I thought I may have had a dud so purchased another one, because I love the way this pencil writes. But after a month (essentially the same amount of time as my first one) the inner-mechanism broke again and won't feed out led.

I treat my pencils with the utmost care and have never dropped them. This makes me really sad..
Excellent pencil. The lead retracts when you press the pocket clip, so no accidental lead breaks. Has a good weight and will probably last many years.
Loved this pencil for the 6 months I've had it; then today it broke and the grip came off! Sad, as I had expected the quality to be much better, especially considering the cost!

Where has this thing been all my life?! This is honestly the best mechanical pencil I've ever used. It's sturdy, well balanced, and so comfortable to hold. Drawing has never been more comfortable. I love that the pencil is  retractable (push the clip), so you don't have to worry about your point breaking or possibly poking through something if you toss it in a bag or in your pocket. It's also great that these are color coded by size, so you can easily see which size lead the pencil is (.7-blue, .5-black, .9-yellow, .4-green, .3-red). These also have a little window that shows what hardness of lead is in the pencil, which you can set by turning the pencil grip until it shows the correct type (H, HB, B, 2B). The erasers on these are surprisingly good. The eraser is hidden under the button, all you have to do is pull the little cap off. The eraser is small, but you can buy replacements if needed (I think they come in a tube of 4 or 5). I don't use the leads that come with them, since I prefer Faber-Castell or Staedtler leads for drawing. You can use any brand of lead you like as long as it's the right size.

Great feel, great function, great look. Don't let my rating fool you, I love this pencil. The rating reflects the cheap construction of this pencil for the price you pay, and for that I must say shame on you Pentel for making such a cheap product. I have bought two of these now because the plastic tube that makes the center section of the pencil has broken. If the pencil had been constructed as the one I now have or at least similar to it (which is explained below), my rating would have been 5 stars. By the same token, if I hadn't been able to fix at least one of the two I bought the rating would have been 1 star.

As an engineer this pencil has been indispensable to me. But while I may be an engineer, I do a lot of hands on and heavy work.

The way Pentel designed the junction between the upper tube and the lower plastic body (the part under the rubber and metal finger grip) causes a major stress point and, in the case of my first one, after only having had it for a few months just the force of lightly leaning against a table while it was in my pocket was enough to break the plastic tube and literally break the pencil in half. A similar event occured with the second one I bought but happened within 3 weeks of me buying it.

Considering how expensive these are I was not about to buy a third and I tried several times to glue the two pieces back together to no avail. Whatever plastic Pentel used does not like to be glued as every time I did, it survived for less time than the previous. Fortunately my father does machining as part of one of his hobbies and was able to make a substitute piece out of brass to replicate and replace the broken plastic. The pencil has since stood up to quite a lot of punishment and still works great.

So once again Pentel, for what you charge for this pencil it should have been constructed A LOT BETTER than it is.

Feels good and writes superior. This is my goto woodshop pencil. I have it in .5,.7 and .9 and use it daily. I also love the retraction feature keeping me from snapping them constantly. Well made even if you toss stuff around the shop like i do. Highly recommend over the dollar carpenters pencil.

t: Well at least it look good.....
x: The plastic components inside the pencil broke after a couple months of daily use.  Very disappointed as I really liked this pencil.

t: Lead stopped pushing through after one month of use.
x: I have always really liked most of the Pentel pencils I have used in the past, and I was looking for new pencil with a metal grip to use during tests for school. This seemed to fit the bill perfectly even though I thought it was a bit pricey. The problem is that the lead stopped coming out after only a month of use. No, this is not a refill problem. I use other 0.5mm Pentel pencils, refill them with Pentel 0.5mmm super hi-polymer lead HB, and I have not encountered this problem with any of the other models. This is unacceptable to have a pencil which costs this much and breaks within a month of use. Otherwise, I really liked this pencil. The grip  is quite nice and I love that it gives the option of displaying which lead you are currently using. I was not a fan of the small eraser; however, if that had been the only problem it would have received a 4-star review from me.
This mechanical pencil is the best to draw and write with.  I use the 0.9mm leads and it doesn't break or tear the paper.

There are four different sizes.  I love that they are color matched by size, but more importantly the lead size is printed in a big number on the top of the cap (nice attn to detail).  It's very cool that when you press on the clip to put it in a pocket, it automagically snaps the lead and tip into the pencil, and when you click on the cap once, it restores the lead and tip to their last setting.

This is just about as perfect as it gets. The weight of the pencil is hefty without being overburdening. The retractable tip is excellent as well and has probably already saved myn from demise.

My only wish would be for it to include a auto-rotational device so that the lead wears evenly and does not break. This is problem that is common among most mechanical pencils, so you can't entirely blame The Pentel Graph Gear 1000.

I use mechanical pencils a lot - many for very specific duties including technical drawings, drafting, etc. - mostly 2.0mm leads. But, needing one for everyday carry, this one is good. Pentel has been making writing instruments forever. The textured grip is very effective without being uncomfortable, and the clip feels like it is not going to snap off any time soon - something that can't be said for much of the competition. Another nice feature that is not as common as one would hope is having the lead size prominently visible on both the barrel and end of the pencil. Very important if/when one needs to have different lead diameters for different tasks.

My only complaint (and it big enough to take away a full star) is that the point is not "pocket-friendly" - meaning that, even with the lead retracted, you're going to end up with a hole in your shirt pocket...... sooner rather than later. Mine is always in a briefcase slot, so I knew going in that this is not a pencil that you want to carry in your pocket day-in and day-out. If that is important to you, find one of the other brands that retracts not only the lead, but also the tiny sleeve that grips the lead.

UPDATE 8/14/2020 - I found a way to retract the lead AND the thin sleeve that grips it - thus allowing the pencil to "pocket-friendly". Notice that when you advance the lead by pressing the cap on the end of the pencil, the clip also snaps in place. To retract the lead AND the sleeve, just push the top end of the clip and everything will pull back in, and solve the hole-making problem. So now a 5-star rating.

t: I normally use 7 mm lead on cheap plastic pencils because the 5mm lead breaks too easily with a cheap pencil - not so with this
x: I have both the 7 mm and the 5 mm.  I use these everyday.  I normally use 7 mm lead on cheap plastic pencils because the 5mm lead breaks too easily with a cheap pencil - not so with this pencil.  The 5 mm will not break and is much sharper than the 7mm.

I love this pencil, I once dropped one on an international flight and stayed behind after we landed just to reclaim it.
It's heavy but not too heavy, the lead takes some finesse to not break but once you get the pressure down it feels great (plus most people won't try and steal it because of this)

t: Great pencil for Engineering students, but buy a separate eraser.
x:
Engineering student and love this pencil!

Pros: The metal tip retracts to prevent breaking. It’s definitely an upgrade from the Graph Gear 500. The pencil writes smooth as butta’.

Cons: Awww snap! The lead it comes with is better. I used some cheap lead replacements and the lead snaps more often now. Also, this stubby eraser ain’t good for nothin’! These two factors lead to the minus one star.

The take away: For a student that is constantly writing pages and pages of notes and equations, this is an excellent upgrade just be sure to buy a separate eraser.
It's a bit heavy, so it breaks when dropped hard.

t: Great pencil but be wary for an EDC.
x:
I bought this as an every day carry pocket pencil. The retractable tip is ideal to avoid stabbing yourself. It lasted for 4 months before the barrel broke right where the finger grip threads on.

I had high hopes for this and absolutely loved it until it broke. Id be fine with if it lasted a couple of years instead of 4 months. I can't justify buying 3 of these a year.

t: It was really good but broke!
x: While I had it, It was a really nice pencil which sadly broke on me. It practically snapped in half, the tip / thing that twists the entire pencil together broke and so it doesn’t come together anymore. Pretty upset for a pretty expensive mechanical pencil.

I've been writing with 0.3mm pencils for about 30 years and this is one of the best I've used. It's solid and reliable, doesn't jam or break leads, the tip - which is always delicate on 0.3mm pencils - retracts, and it has tight tolerances so the tip doesn't jiggle when it's deployed for writing. Works best with "B" lead, which gives a dark line without pressing too hard which tends to break 0.3 lead. The price hovers around $15 and you just can't beat that because cheaper pencils jam, break leads, and fall apart. I own 4 of them - 3 for me (home, work and travel), 1 for my daughter.

t: Amazing pencil that has never had a lead break for me
x:
I was a little hesitant paying almost $10 for a pencil, but as an engineer I need one often and I got tired of lead breaking, etc. This pencil is fantastic. I'm using Ain Stein 0.7 mm HB primarily as the lead but I also have some 0.7 mm H. The only thing I wish is that I had gotten 0.5 mm, but that is nothing against the pencil itself. I'll probably buy a 0.5 after this review.

If you're thinking about buying this pencil, go ahead and do it. If you're in the market for a better pencil with lead that doesn't break while writing, definitely buy this pencil.

Ok thats corny, I'm sorry. This pencil is worth every single penny! I get compliments on it all the time. blah blah blah I can say all kinds of cool things about it, how about I just make a list!
- the balance is great
- fits and feels nice in the hand
- the clip doesn't touch the web of your hand! I usually break them off of pens and pencils because I hate that poking. When I saw this had a clip i was upset until i used it. ok back to list making!
- retractable tip so you don't get shanked
-cool colors and a cheap rubber pads
- style style style
- the clicker end fits perfectly right inside your lip for hands free transport of the pencil, fits ike a cigarette, only more comfortable, contoured and not at all deadly.
- will last forever

ok and to be fair here are the cons
- people will see this and think you're a math or engineering genius.
- you'll wanna get high quality lead, don't get the walmart or target brand, get pentel super polymer lead, I use 2B for ink-like dark lines
-hmm whats another con.....? Martha Stewart!

Buy this pencil, it'll improve your penmanship [citation needed]which make you happier. So be happy, buy the pencil and prosper.
A great pencil! The lead is so strong and dosent break.

Although I really liked the feel of this pencil in my hand, the mechanism to push the lead through the pencil breaks easily (it doesn't push the lead through not matter how much you abuse the push button...). My first pencil broke in less than 30 days and the second broke about 2 months after I replaced the first one. It also took me a while to figure out that the push button can come off to reveal an eraser and when pulling out the eraser, the end to put extra lead in. Packaging was not ideal (the pencil was just thrown into a box) but it came in one piece and undamaged. I will not recommend this pencil since there is something seriously wrong with the design of the mechanism.

It works. It has a metal tip that holds the lead securely. I usually broke the lead of my previous pencils or the lead would fall out. That hassle is gone.

I put a bumper on the pencil to make the grip area fatter. It is fine without the bumper but I prefer a fatter grip/

Look good too.

Well worth my money. My lead no longer breaks constantly. I don't have to worry about the tip bending because the tip retracts when you clip it to your pocket! It's perfect for when I'm doing math, drawing and writing. This is probably my favorite thing that I've bought on impulse. :)

t: Nice pencil, cheap parts, will break
x: As noted earlier, the cheap plastic part inside the pencil snapped after 12 months of use. I do not recommend this

t: It closes all the way led and pointer so it won’t poke you if you have pockets
x: Lead is strong and won’t keep breaking when you use it I recommend this to anyone

t: It broke couple of month after purchase
x: I bought it a couple of month ago, it was great, I loved this pensive, but yesterday wile in class it just broke I was re tightens the front peice and it broke. I hope I could get send a replacment and change this bad experience.

I liked the feel and the weight of the pencil, but the lead broke often if just a bit too far out, and it had to be advanced more often than I liked.  It seemed sturdy and well made, but the internal lead-advancement mechanism stopped working so the whole thing is unusable now.  I only purchased it in late 2016, and it never left my home office desk, and in under two years it is done.  It never even used up all the lead that came in it, or the original eraser.  I think it should have lasted much longer with the little use it got, and was never abused or carried around, for the price and apparent quality.  It is too bad that it is not fixable; I would have liked to fix it rather than have to throw it out.

t: Used to be my favorite, but quality issues!
x:
I used to have these for every size. Recently, though, my 0.9 mm pencil snapped at the yellow plastic portion halfway along the shaft. It was shocking as this occurred simply in the normal process of writing.

They were worth the price until this became a possibility. Now I'm shopping for something else.

t: The best pencil I have ever owned.
x: This is honestly the best pencil I have ever owned.  It is strong, doesn't break down.  I wish it had a larger eraser, but that is kind of impossible given the quality of this pencil and its size.  The gnarled grip with the rubber circles is perfect and I love how you can retract the tip so your led doesn't break and your pencil doesn't get damaged.

t: Wonderful, Sturdy Build.  Never breaks (I'm a hard writer).
x: Best mechanical pencil I've ever had.  Lead does not break.  Firmly retracts with clip on top.  Longer than usual eraser in the back under the metal cap.  I wish I knew about this line sooner.  I've ordered the 0.7mm as well and plan to throw away or donate some bic plastic ones I have.  I wish there was a 0.8 mm.  I break the 0.7's too easily and the 0.9's aren't precise enough.  But given the standards as they are no one can knock this pencil.  Beware - this is a heavy pencil.  Smaller-handed people may not like it.  The grip is part metal, part plastic (or hard rubber...).  Some may find that uncomfortable.  Again.  Just beautiful.  I'd pay $20 for good quality stuff like this that I am confident will go the distance.  Worked like a charm through a 3 hour finance exam.

I'm hoping the seller sees this review.

The pencil itself is a great pencil. It's extremely sturdy, feels great to hold. It definitely helps prevent lead breakage while writing. Being metal, it's darn impossible to break off the clip which is common for those plastic ones.

My only complaint is how they (don't) package the item. When you get shipped the pencil, it has the tag/barcode on the pencil and it ships in a pathetic plastic bag.

If you're spending $16 on a mechanical pencil, I'd expect it to be shipped in one of those pen holder boxes; give it some value.
LOVE this pencil! This is my go to pencil every time I draw. feels nice in the hand and the lead is nice an strong and doesn't break off like most mechanical pencils do.
Broke after using it a few times

When I first got the pencil, it arrived without any protective packaging and with the bottom slightly bent. The pencil was still usable, but the bend made it essentially impossible to write consistently as lead would constantly break as it could not conform to the bent structure of the pencil. Two weeks in, and now it completely broke. The end of the pencil is completely bent to the side and lead will refuse to come out for writing. I do not recommend buying this.

I love this pencil so much more than I ever thought possible to love a pencil. The body is really sleek and sexy. The grip is nice and comfortable without being awkward or bulky. And the best part is the retracting tip. It's so cool! When you push on the clip to open it up, the tip snaps back so you don't stab yourself with a pencil in your pocket. I spent a pretty absurd amount of time just playing with that feature. The eraser also works really well (it's under the metal cap). It's pretty small in diameter (I like that, it's much more precise) but it's actually fairly long, and replacements are pretty cheap.

t: This a very nice and great mechanical pencil to write and everything
x: This a very nice and great mechanical pencil to write and everything. The only flaw is that it seems to break down after a few months of usage.

I wanted a metal pencil that would last. Others that I have purchased usually broke after a few weeks; this pencil is still going strong after several months. The weight of it is just right, and the 0.9mm lead is perfect for me.
Came in broken! I was so disappointed. I was planning to give it as a gift. With covid returns is hard for me.

t: Love this pencil, but the build quality disappoints
x:
Pentel has always previously delivered in quality since I've started using them 30+ years ago. I've had two of out of three of these Graphgear pencils break on me within the first year of usage: one at the plastic join near the middle of the barrel and the other at the tip. I really love the design, feel, and performance of this pencil....WHEN IT DOESN'T BREAK. Out of the probably 3-4 dozen Pentels I've owned over the years, these are the first to ever break.

I really want to love this pencil, but the quality disappoints.

t: too much 'clicking and clearing' - get the .5mm! use it with "hb" lead sticks.
x:
The lead breaks way too easily, and jams the pencil constantly. Every 5 to 10 minutes of writing needed 2 minutes of click-advancing, and 6 minutes of fixing.That is a bad combination.
I was snapping lead as i wrote, but I adjusted my pencil grip and angle. At least SOMETHING was solved.
However, lead would break inside the pencil, and block a replacement from feeding.
For every 3 sentences I wrote, I spent 6 minutes "clicking and clearing" a 5mm piece of lead.
All the other reviewers that said the pencil quit working, were really experiencing the same thing, I believe.

I just used the little wire stuck in the eraser to poke the lead back in the pencil, and out the back. (GEE, guess why THAT is there...?)
The pencil then works until the new lead breaks again. I am moving up to .5mmm (already have .7 and wanted thinner lead)

update:
YMMV, but the .5mm is perfect for me. Still a thin line, but no bs. I am able to write more than one sentence before I have to advance the lead again, and it does NOT break. Well worth it for me. (I didnt return the .3 I dont believe in that, but it is now relegated to waiting for a pencil sketch that needs very light feathering)

t: Nice pencil with a short lifespan
x:
I have bought three of these 0.3 millimeter pencils and two of them have failed in the exact same way. The inner plastic sleeve breaks which causes the pencil to fall apart and become useless.

I really wish the manufacturer would make an all-metal version of this pencil that is more durable. I would be happy to pay for a better quality pencil if it means it lasts more than a few months.

t: Writes nice, but broke in half when I dropped it.
x: I like the pencil for writing or drawing.  Love the weight of it, but I dropped it on the floor and it broke in half.  The metal casing looks so robust, but there is only plastic holding it together.  That said, I do like it enough that I did repurchase.
So glad I bought this.  So much better than the disposable garbage.  A++

t: That yellow bit there? That is threaded plastic holding ...
x: That yellow bit there? That is threaded plastic holding metal. Eventually the stress will cause the plastic to break. Happened to 3 of these in a row. Buy a different mechanical pencil

t: I have nothing to say but I love it! Engineered so beautifully
x:
After using this pencil for about THREE years, I have nothing to say but I love it!
Engineered so beautifully!
The tip itself can hide inside the cases - never had any of the graphite broken!
Rubber grips are very comfortable to write and sketch whole day!
Mechanical Engineering area says thank you Pentel for providing such a gorgeous tool to make ideas drawn with so many details.

t: Please let me know of my review was helpful!
x: I'm going to start off by saying that this is by far one of my favorite pencils.  I recently purchased a rotring 600 (~$40) and I prefer this pentel over that one, which is slightly unfortunate.  One of my favorite features is the knock back tip.  I love having a sturdy, one piece tip that won't break my lead.  I usually don't get them however, due to the fact that they usually end up stabbing my leg.  This is not the case with the Pentel Graph gear 1000.  Looks good and writes comfortably.
My mech pencil came with a bent tip,because of this the lead frequently breaks making a terrible experience.
I used this for a while then the plastic part snapped.
This product was bad. Broke and led gets stuck. Do not buy!!

t: Such a unique pencil, this has become my daily ...
x: Such a unique pencil, this has become my daily driver for drawing. I can put this in my pocket and not be afraid of it breaking because it is made of metal. The part that holds the lead retracts back into the pencil so it can't break when not in use which is something I didn't even think was possible! I plan on buying the smaller lead sizes at a later date.

After trying numerous mechanical pencils, ranging in price from this to a stylish one for $300, I returned to this.

Pros: Nice balance, easy to hold.
Comfortable grip, which I was worried about because of the scoring of the metal, but the silicone bumps take care of that.
Retractable point.
Easily accessed eraser.
Extended lead holder to prevent breakage.
Ability to identify which hardness is in the pen.
Stylish design for a mechanical pencil.

Cons: None.

That pretty much says it.

I am very pleased with this mechanical pencil.  It's comfortable to hold, and I don't break and waste lead like I do with other pencils.  In the picture, it looks like the barrel grip is rubber, but it's metal and makes the pencil very attractive.  At least four people have commented on how professional the pencil looks, and I really like how easy it is to advance the lead with a single click.  Retracting the tip into the barrel is a big plus, too.  You won't go wrong with this one.

t: Pretty good pencil, especially compared to the Rotwing 800.
x:
I've owned both a Rotwing 800, Uni KuruToga Roulette, and this pencil.
And to be honest with you? I think I like this one the best. It's just simple enough to do it's job, and feels and looks fancy like the rotwings do.
And it won't break in 2 drops like the rotwing did with me. I'm satisfied. :)

If you're in the market for a mechanical pencil, get either this, or the Uni KuruToga Roulette, or both!

As a Drafting instructor, you tend to use pencils a lot. I have many mechanical pencils I acquired while in engineering school. The Pentel Graph Gear 1000 is the best balanced mechanical pencil I have ever used.
The clip is something you need to get used to. It serves as a clip for the pocket and it also locks the .5mm metal point out
of the larger barrel. The inter barrel slides in to the pen for safe keeping.
I recommend the Pentel Graph Gear 1000 to anyone who is in drafting, engineering or even art.
The pen is heavy because it is made of metal.

The only issue I have is the way the pencil was shipped to me. It came in a large box that contained an X-Acto sharpener I ordered. The Pencil was put in the box as is with no protection. Someone at Amazon need to have a talk with the shipping guys. The Pencil could have been broken but thank got it was not.

I hate writing with pencil-sharpener type pencils.  After 2-3 words, the lead starts spreading and I need to write small.  I tried the disposable mechanicals, but the lead is cheap and frequently breaks.  These are the pencil equivalent of rapidograph pens, a specific lead thickness and the Pentel people have quality leads that don't break easily.  The mechanism that extends and retracts the point saves you from pocket damage from the tip.

t: Awesome pencil for a great price
x:
Hands down best mechanical pencil I've ever owned. This is the third time I've purchased it since someone broke it the first time and I lost it the second time.

It's comfortable to hold and very eye-catching. I'd highly recommend this as a daily-driver pencil.

Not everyone needs or likes mechanical pencils, but if you do, this is a great choice. I bought this on sale out of curiosity having heard others talk about it with wildly different opinions. (How can people be passionate about something as trivial as a pencil? I don't know, but here we are in any case.) Bottom line: I found I like it much better than the cheaper Pentel 207 and similar.

PROs: It feels substantial, but not too heavy. The buttons on the knurling look strange, but they improve the grip. it seems solid and well-built, and it looks and feels like it is over-engineered (which appeals to a certain kind of person, while others could care less). The metal sleeve and precision advancement mean you break the lead less frequently. By pressing the clip, you can pop the sharp part back into the barrel which protects the tip and keeps it from poking holes in your pockets or sticking you when you carry it. It also looks more slim in real life than it does in many of the images. Plus it's really cheap compared to many high-end pencils.

CONs: Some on-line reviews say the tip is often loose and that the barrel breaks with extended use. The tip on the one I received is not loose, and I think you would have to be pretty heavy-handed to actually break the barrel, but I haven't had it very long and time may change my mind. In any case, it's only a couple of bucks. Odds are I'll lose it before I break it, and I'd much rather lose one at this price than many of the more expensive ones. I'll run the risk.

t: I am in love with a pencil!
x: I absolutely LOVE this set!. I actually purchased the 0.3 Pentel GraphGear after using these mechanical pencils because I had to have the whole range. The pencil is very easy to handle, very comfortable in the hand, and writes very smoothly. I really like how the point pops in when you press the pocket clip. I like how easy the lead is to advance using the top, and the fact that you don't potentially dump out all of your lead when you want to get at the eraser. The small sized eraser enables you to erase or highlight very small sections of your work, which is a plus. The leads themselves are very sturdy, very little breakage, and what there was, was my fault for extending the lead too far out. I appreciate being able to use different hardness of leads and having an indicator on the pencil to set to remind me what I am using. I also love the use of rubberized colored dots on the barrel to let you know the size lead the pencil uses, and how the rubber dots make it easy to hold for long lengths of time. I am enclosing a picture I drew entirely with the .3 pencil on Strathmore 5.5 x 8.5 toned tan sketch paper. I used all the lead that came pre-loaded in the pencil, plus two more pieces that were included in the set. I worked sometimes for hours on this without any hand strain at all. I highly recommend this pencil to anyone. The affordable price means you don't have that much to lose, and with this whole set, you are good to go for a long time if you love it as much as I do.

Very solid construction, well put together.  I had to clean out the mechanism at first because of the thin size of the leads one had broken inside but other than that this has worked flawlessly and I use it nearly every day.  Highly recommended.

Love this automatic pencil.  With the slightly thicker lead it works great in the shop and everywhere else.  I have a couple, however, I dropped one off a counter top onto a concrete floor and it snapped clean in half!

t: Broke in a couple of months. Ordered a new one which broke again. Don't recommend.
x:
I liked this pencil, but it broke after a couple months of use after dropping it from desk height. I liked it so much I bought another one, but this one broke as well after dropping it from desk height.

I won't be getting another because they break too easily.
Great pen! However mine broke a few months in and it was a disappointing moment.

Love these pencils. I bought one and it lasted 10 years before the plastic inside snapped. These are some of the best mechanical pencils on the market.

I am an artist and almost exclusively use these for sketching.

t: but for those of you who like to press hard when they write
x: This pencil will change your life! Never have I ever had such a well-designed writing utensil. It's a bit on the heavier side, but for those of you who like to press hard when they write, this pencil does an excellent job in preventing the lead from breaking. Also love the retractable tip!

t: Barrel Snapped down the middle after normal use
x:
This pencil worked great until the barrel unceremoniously snapped one day. I believe this pencil lasted 6 months and was never used roughly. The threaded portion of the grip portion of the barrel is still broken off inside so this cannot even be repaired.

I would suggest that if durability is important feature to look elsewhere, was surprised to break a seemingly all metal pencil so easily

I really like the design of this pencil. It has great weight, not too heavy but not light as a feather either. Its comfortable to hold with the knurled grip and small rubber insets. I love that the tip retracts. However, I would warn that if you’re looking to use it as an every day writer you might want to jump up to the 0.5 or 0.7mm.  I found the lead would break off quite a bit when writing, which is aggravating. It would also break and get stuck inside the barrel, causing it to jam frequently. I was using the Pentel Ain Stein 0.3mm lead, so I know it wasn’t a problem of cheap refills. While I do prefer a fine tip for my writing utensils, I just found this 0.3mm lead to be too fine for my main writer. I’m giving this a 4 star rating because of the design but I have to knock off a point for execution. I replaced this with the 0.7 and it works absolutely fantastic as an an every day writer. It still has that fine tip feel without the frailty of the 0.3mm.
I love this pencil but one thing the lead breaks to easy make a harder HB lead

t: Best mechanical pencils in the universe they are so good ...
x: Best mechanical pencils in the universe they are so good build quality is amazing they only way I broke my last one was when I ran it over with my car on accident but went back and bought more cause they are so amazing!

t: Pentel Graph Gear 1000 Automatic Drafting Pencil
x: I purchased the pencil to use for dimensional marking in wood-working. Pentel is a brand well-known for their mechanical pencils, however this pencil, while solid-metal construction and "stout" feeling, has NOT measured up - for me - especially for the price. It was, from day-one, prone to not extending lead and now won't extend lead "at-all". Broken with only short-term light use. Perhaps due to my use, which is again, wood-working, but the pencil was never abused, and (for the third time) was only used for a very short time before it "quit". For the money and the Pentel name, I certainly expected more......

t: Broke in a month - lousy customer service
x: This pencil feels great; I love the balance and weight. Unfortunately, my pencil stopped feeding lead after about a month of use. I contacted Pentel about the issue and the resolution was for me to pay to return the defective item for repair. To me, it's not worth spending several dollars to return a $10 pencil. I just spent that money to buy a different brand. They are working great.

Got the .3mm. The pencil fits nicely and you can definitely feel the quality. The withdraw action is nice and the feeding mechanism is pretty reliable, though like in all the mechanical pencils I use the lead sometimes breaks in the tip and causes clogs.
Feels very solid. Prevents lead breakage by only putting out a little bit per click. The pocket clip making the tip retract is genius.

Using this pencil is a delight, overall my art has drastically increased since I've started using this pencil, and of course, the lead is very easy to break since it measures .3mm, but that isn't the pencil's fault more the user. It taught me to use lighter strokes when drawing as I worked with it.

I've owned two of these now. The first I had for two years before the plastic sleeve under the barrel snapped. The second arrived two weeks ago. Others have really detailed these pencils well, so look at their posts for depth. I'll just tell you my quick opinion on them.

One thing I just have to say about these, beyond the great polished aluminum look, is the feel! These pencils just feel 'right.' They write amazing, feel amazing, are sturdy, and take common lead+erasers; the perfect pencil.

Get one today, you will not regret it.

Is a little expensive but it well worth it, it highly durable, the first one i bought lasted me about 4-5 years before it broke around plastic that you can move to mark which lead shade you are using. So just be careful not to play too much with the dial, because it can break

I love this pencil, and I bought it back in 2014, as well as a few replacements.  I was disappointed though this morning that it broke right where the smooth part and grip come together... it seems this may be the weak link in it as that is only kept together with plastic.  If it was all metal, it would be perfect, so one star removed, but it lasted until 2022 so that is really good.

I usually bought cheap mechanical pencils because I would usually lose them or let others borrow them and never get them back. I have finally got to a point where I don't lose pencils so I decided to buy a little more expensive one. Overall I love the pencil and would buy another.

Pros:
-Metal and very sturdy
-Retractable tip so the end doesn't break when storing
-Value indicator to label lead hardness

Cons:
-The retracting mechanism sometimes misses the slot and may break later on
-When hands are a little sweaty the grip doesn't grab but metal still does.
-Sticker that says .7 fell off (not a big deal)
The best feature for me is the way the lead does not break easily.

Good sturdy pencil, comfortable to write with. I live the fine point, it is stable. I work in Astroynamics and has lots of fine and small writing and this is perfect. The weight of it is really nice because I don't feel like I'm going to break the pencil in half (I grip tightly).

The title pretty much says it all. I have been buying mechanical pencils since I was 12 years old (1977) and this is the best one I have ever found. I bought ten of them and gave two to my ex-wife (an accountant for a school) and she agrees. Even though it's quite expensive, it's worth every cent. Heavy in your hand (most are too light), nicely textured barrel for excellent grip, feeds beautifully with a tip that retracts so it doesn't jab through your pocket.

And if you can get an ex-wife on board... need I say more?

Pick your favorite size (mine is .7 with the harder "leads" - it writes as sharp as an average .5 but without breaking as much).

Only downside: same lame, tiny eraser you usually get with these. Why can't anyone make a good Dixon Ticonderoga Wood-Cased #2 Pencil-type eraser on a mechanical?

I like having a thin line when I write with mechanical pencils, so I ordered the .3mm. Unfortunately, the lead breaks off whenever I extend it enough to write. I'd recommend a thicker lead. On the pro side, the body of this metal pencil has a nice weight to it.

t: I'd order this again and again. I hope I don't have to, but I would.
x: I had one break after a year of use, but I swear by this pencil. Solid weight and consistent mechanics, plus it's retractable. And the cost is reasonable for all that's packed in this little beast.

t: LOVE. Use it everyday being an electrician
x: LOVE. Use it everyday being an electrician. Easily writes on metal conduit, or PVC. Works on concrete and drywall as well too. The clip is a bit fragile, as I broke my first one, and without the clip the pen is unusable. When you click the back, the inner shaft moves down to the tip to expose the lead, and at the same time the clip clicks into a slot on the inner shaft to keep it locked. To pull the lead back in, press the top of the clip (towards the eraser) and the inner shaft and lead will snap back into place, safely protecting the tip.
Nice to be able to retract the head so you don't constantly break the lead off.

t: My drawings are smarter with this pencil
x:
I feel smarter when i use this pencil. I bought 6 of them. Love em!

They look smart and sexy (in a nerds-are-sexy kinda way).

Clicky, soild, they even have erasers. 1 or 2 of them broke in a weird way: they still work but they don't retract neatly. I don't care though - i still love em.

t: Not for woodworking, Bad company response
x: This is not a product for rough use and the company will not respond. While the pencil has a metal shaft, it has a plastic ring in the middle that holds it together that breaks easily. I liked the 1000, but broke two, one in my shop apron when I leaned on something and the other that dropped on a cement floor and hit at the wrong angle. Both times I have tried to contact Pentel both through their website and by phone and they will NOT RESPOND! $25 for the two of them was wasted. If you read their warranty, it makes it VERY difficult to get a response and they count on you to give up.

The GEL PEN of PENCILS: this mechanical pencil + 2B LEAD = pure heaven

Ended up buying this at an art supply store (and paying way more) because I wanted to try it out in person and needed it the next day. This pencil is AWESOME. I used to HATE pencils, like hate. It always felt like it was like scratching on cardboard. I'm in grad school and wanted to get one NICE pencil since I'd need it for projects. Did a little research and found out both the SIZE and TYPE of LEAD makes a HUGE difference.

-The SOFTER the LEAD the SMOOTHER the writing experience: Hardest: H ---> HB "regular" --> 2B SOFT!***
(also the softer the lead, the darker your mark of the lead will be and the less easily it will break.)
-The LARGER the size of the lead (diameter) the less easily the lead will break: 0.5mm --> 0.7mm (regular)--> 0.9mm*** (largest and Smoothest)

GUIDE to PENCIL LEAD: http://www.jetpens.com/blog/picking-the-perfect-pencil-lead-hardness-grade/pt/475
My 2 favorite ERASERS (smooth like butter + no mess or smearing):
Caran d'Ache Technik: ($3.99 at Dick blick): http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001UNKY5M/ref=cm_cr_rev_prod_title
(Double the size of the Uni Boxy)
Uni Boxy Eraser:
http://www.jetpens.com/Uni-Boxy-Eraser-Black/pd/499
Had this bad boy shipped in from Japan because of its reviews. Not gonna lie it's pretty epic.
Guide to Erasers: http://www.jetpens.com/blog/a-guide-to-erasers/pt/597
Update: I liked it so much I ended up buying the same pencil in the .7mm size on amazon (also got 2B lead) so I could have some variety.
I've shown a few friends this pencil (and the following 2 erasers) and all have gone out and bought them the next day.
One, who's a physics grad student liked it so much he ordered 4 the next day in 1 shot saying he could now toss the pencil sharpener on his desk.

t: Durable and Functional for Everyday Use
x:
I got the 0.5mm version of the Pentel Graph Gear 1000 pencil around December of 2014, so far it has lasted to this day and I expect it to last for years. There hasn't been any other mechanical pencil replacing this. In fact, I even bring this pencil with me to anywhere I expect to be writing. As a student, I'm constantly moving and using this pencil. Usually, the pen gets thrown into my backpack, where my plastic pencils break and my wooden pencils have their tips broken off.

Now, this pencil might seem very pricey, but this depends on the person. I don't abuse my pencils too much, but my plastic mechanical pencils usually break within a few months (specially the Paper Mate Clearpoint pencils), and I end up buying new ones every once in a while. So far, I haven't seen the need to replace the Graph Gear 1000.

My only worries are the clip and plastic internals, but there seems to be no complications so far. The retractable tip and the grip are two features I take for granted, but they help me a lot. I highly recommend this pencil, because it works for the price I pay.
It worked just like it was supposed to! Good weight and very well balanced. Even thought it is a .3 pencil it doesn't break easily. Works really well for drawing fur!!

Relatively cheap, but still not worth it. It feels cheap, and after the first piece of lead was done, I could never get another one to load. Spent 10 minutes trying to get the next piece to load so I could keep writing. I’ve never had this issue with other cheap mechanical pencils. Ended up snapping it in 2 and throwing in the trash.

t: This is the best mechanical pencil I've ever had the pleasure of using.
x:
I first got one over a year ago and it lasted me an entire school year of daily use. Sure, there was some degradation over time, but I would be questioning it's earthly origin if it didn't... but I digress.
The pencil is wonderfully weighted, it feels amazing in your hand. The clip is tremendously strong and the grip feels great. Recently it finally broke where the two halves connect, the fact that it took this long gives me reason to speak incredibly highly of this pencil. When it broke, I immediately bought a new one. I almost feel like I can no longer live without this pencil.

t: Uses less lead due to inovative design.
x: This is the finest pencil I've ever used, including cartography pencils in college.  The weight is perfect in hand and well balanced.  As you click lead out of the pencil the pocket clip depresses. Apply pressure to the pocket clip  and it releases an internal mechanism that retracts the exposed lead back into the pencil barrel. This eliminates unnecessary lead breakage and keeps the sharp lead in the barrel where it belongs; ingenious! There's also a rotating  indicator on the barrel that indicates what kind of lead is being used. Super  if you are using more than one lead type. Just an exceptional pencil. I use mine on the trapline taking notes and recording catches. Will be buying a couple more to have on hand. Well worth the money.

t: An Excellent Mechanical Pencil; but improvements theoretically possible
x:
This is an excellent mechanical pencil. It's one you buy to keep; not use and dispose of. Undergraduate students looked at it with awe and respect (just kidding there- let's not get carried away). It's very functional, but not the overt display of opulence of products made by jewelers.
It writes very well, and has good balance. The grip has that knurled surface that prevents it from slipping around when, for example, your hands are wet or dirty. The action advancing the pencil leads is flawless.. Pencil leads can break when too much lateral pressure is applied, but it requires more than most other mechanical pencils. The process of refilling leads is good. No problems there.
I like the design of that spring-loaded clip. You ever find yourself upside-down when you didn't expect it? It stays put in your shirtpocket or when clipped to your shirt's collar.
After ~3-5 years I noticed some corrosion on the barrel of one i purchased. This occurred after repeated exposure to humidity from being on the bathroom counter near the shower. You wouldn't have that problem with plastic. Some of the graphics looked weathered due to wear. Could the black graphics be etched into the barrel? Who knows how much a pencil like this would cost, however.
The only weakness is that the eraser inside it (underneath the cap) tends to slide back when pressure is applied. This doesn't happen with the eraser from the factory, but after I installed refills. The eraser holding bracket just didn't grip enough (anymore) after installing refill erasers. And so the eraser didn't stay put;' making erasure difficult and frustrating. I know it's my own fault, with big Trump-like hands. After putting in a new eraser, I couldn't re-form that bracket exactly again. I believe that some writers might never use that eraser, opting instead for a separate one.
Overall, a great product for those who need better than just a cheap throwaway pencil.

t: THE LAST MECHANICAL PENCIL YOU WILL EVER NEED
x:
I have over 10 different mechanical pencils I have purchased because I have been in a search for the most perfect mechanical pencil. Basically I needed one that didn't break after time didn't cause the led to break all the time, and most importantly: was comfortable to grab and didn't slide through my fingers.

I highly recommend this mechanical pencil, simply due to its knarled grip which will make it so the pencil won't slip through your fingers. Also, the Lead tip retracts when you click the pencil, so you won't stab your backpack or pocket. I only wished this pencil had a larger eraser, but since it is a drafting pencil it has one of those small erasers under the cap.

t: Quality seems to have deteriorated over the years
x:
I’ve been using these pencils for about 6 years now and they’ve been my all time favorite of any brand. They are phenomenal to hold, use, and write with for extended periods of time.

However, I don’t know if I can continue to recommend them. I’ve had two of them break this year with my last one only lasting like 3 months. I’m concerned there is a quality control issue going on with newer fabrications. Either that or I’ve gotten astronomically unlucky.

In short pencil is amazing, but they keep breaking frequently now (within months) when I’ve had prior purchases of this same product last years and I’m not sure if I will be purchasing another one.

t: Not as sturdy as it looks
x:
When the Pentel Graph Gear 100 arrived I was ecstatic. It was tough, reliable, didn't leave holes in my pockets, and was just a great pen to hold and to show off.

And while it worked it was a charm, I took it with me everywhere. However it has one major drawback, and that is the pocket clip. After two months of having in my pocket, the clip broke off, and unlike other pens/pencils, that means that the entire device is useless. The pocket clip keeps holds the tip in place when in use, and hides it when depressed. Graphite would not come out of the tip after the clip broke.

It is a good thing I still carry cheap bic pencils, some have withstood nearly a decade of use. This is a shame, because if it was more durable the Pentel Graph Gear 1000 would be perfect. Come on guys, at least give me a years use for the money.

t: Great pencil, especially for the price
x: A very sturdy mechanical pencil. I like the lead size (0.5 mm) as it allows me to write small and neatly. The pencil itself is quite heavy compared to most plastic mechanical pencils. You will want to buy extra lead, as it can break easily. The eraser is okay but nothing great, so you might want to get a standalone eraser to substitute the built in one. If you're in any sort of technical field (engineering, drafting, architecture, etc) I recommend this pencil. Very reliable and durable.

t: Needs some quality control or something. Pentel junk.
x:
Pencil worked well for a.couple of weeks other than the loose eraser cap. Then it started not retracting fully. The lead kept catching on fingers and edges when it should have been retracted. Emailed customer support and they wanted me to send it back to them in a padded envelope. Not paying at minimum 1/4 of price for maybe getting a repaired or new pencil. They thought it was a pen in the first email I got back even after me telling them the type and model number. No thanks. Plenty of other drafting pencils out there.
July 27th Update: pencil has now fully broken and will not push out more lead. Throwing away.

I have the .5, .7, and the .9 Pentel GraphGear pencils and love them. I keep the .7 and.9 in my wood shop which actually work well when you want a fine mark on wood, and I keep the .5 with my graph pad for when I’m drawing out plans. I love that the ends retract up into the pencils so you don’t have to worry about them getting bent or breaking off if they drop or if you put them in your pocket.I would highly recommend these to anyone who is looking for a good quality mechanical pencil. They are a little pricey but are well worth it.
Great pencil and the lead is hard to break

t: Tip breaks, and autofeed won't using 2B
x:
I purchased 2. Love them with two exceptions. I use only 2B. This may influence my specific results.
1) The tip breaks off frequently as compared to a few other pencils I have. The narrow metal tip seems to bend enough or maybe the edge of the metal point is sharp enough to allow the led tip to break off.
2) As with many pencils, after a time, I am unable to get the next led to autofeed. Each time I instead take it apart and throw away 1/2 a led.
I no longer use this pencil and am looking for alternatives.

Lead does not stay in place once it is about 2/3 used, and the lead always gets stuck inside the pencil so you have to deconstruct the entire thing to get the lead out then put it back together to load new lead and click forever hoping you might get lucky and the lead will properly load. This pencil feels great but is not a great option because it breaks a lot. I almost returned it but I really love how it writes! Just annoying once it runs out of lead.

This pencil is fantastic. I was a fan of the Graph Gear 500 for its lightweight feel, but I bent one too many tips of them. The 1000 solves that problem effortlessly, as the whole mechanism snaps back into the safety of the metal barrel when you flick the clip up. That feature alone has probably saved me having to buy several pencils! I've gotten tons of complements on these pencils, and find that I don't let them out of my sight because I like them so much and because of their shiny silver color, so I'm no longer losing pencils on a regular basis. I may have spent more for these pencils, but I'm still probably spending the same amount of money on pencils, because I protect these more!

(Addendum: If I leave them someplace, people return them to me and are impressed by them.)

Having been a huge fan of the KOH-I-NOOR 5mm mechanical (and later, the Arvin Draft Matic), I just discovered the Graph Gear 1000 a couple of months back. My big issue with the Koh-I-Noor was that the end of the lead holder was prone to bending. Once the end of the barrel was no longer exactly true, the lead would break while coming out and the pencil was useless.  The "1000" has gone five months now, outlasting any of my past pencils. Add to that the cushioned grip and cool retracting mechanism and you've got an awesome product at a fair price.

t: The BEST Mechanical Pencil I EVER HAD! Hands Down
x:
This is hands down the best Mechanical Pencil I have ever owned.

Build quality is excellent and it makes you WANT to draw more and sketch more!

wish it was a bigger eraser to be honest, lol but watever. Not nearly a deal breaker

Great pencil, but I broke it after repeatidly messing with it.  I for some reason like to unscrew and screw the body of evey pen or pencil I have ever used and the plastic incert wore out one day when I was tightining it beyond its limit.

t: Nice Pencil, But Not Too Comfy
x: I got this pencil, because it seem to be a great quality looking pencil. I'd say its nice, but not great. The body is metal, and its heavy for a pencil, balanced at the middle. It breaks up into many parts and has a nice long eraser, that is refillable. However the grip isn't that great, and is still slippery, and the inside is plastic, so not too too strong, and the weak point, i'd say, is the clip. Its a pretty good clip, but can shift to an angle side to side and if it goes, the pencil will no longer work, for it is the clip that holds the retractable tip down. Without it, the pencil will remain retracted for good. Its a nice pencil, that looks good and feels secure, but really isn't, and the weight and grip make it uncomfortable.

These pencils are a little on the expensive side but they are worth it.  I use them in my woodworking shop and I love them.  One push and the correct amount of lead is fed out.  A click on the clip and everything retracts back into the body of the pencil.  They feel good in my hand and I no longer have to worry about lead breaking.  These pencils are well made and a pleasure to use.

Balance is a little too far back which can make your hand grow tired if you're really writing for extended periods of time. Lead indicator is nice as well as the knurled grip is very good. Solid clip that it used to retract tip. There is a little play with the tip which does help so the lead doesn't break as often but can be a little distracting at times. I would recommend this for a carry around pencil since it has a retractable tip but the pentel graph gear 500 is better for at home use as it has a much better balance.

t: Based on the reviews, I got a defective product.
x: I decided to go for this pencil due to all the reviews, sadly it was not what it seemed. I've had 4 exams with these pencil and in every single one. and it just gave me problems, from the lead break immediately to just it not wanting to come out

t: Best mechanical pencil I've ever owned
x: Best mechanical pencil I've ever owned. Never thought I'd be able to use .5 mm lead without breaking it every 15 minutes. It's worth the $10.

t: Excellent build and heavy feel but .3 tips break too easily for me.
x: Maybe it's me that presses down too hard but with the fine point this has it breaks all the time wether I use just a few clicks or a longer point.  It's probably a great pencil for some because it's well made, maybe I just need a thicker pencil style but unless you press lightly the tips break.  I didn't want to leave a bad review because otherwise it seems top notch so maybe lighter users will love it but I need something with stronger tips.  Honestly I think I just need to go up to .5 or .7 and probably will buy this again in those sizes because otherwise this is beautifully built, nice and heavy metal.

This is a great mechanical pencil. Within minutes of getting it I had it fully taken apart to see how it works. It's a very good design and I can't see it breaking or wearing out any time soon. The retractable tip is a nice feature to keep it protected (I've bent lower-end Graphgear pencil tips) and the grip is good, though I put a piece of paper between the silicone grip and the barrel beneath it so it sticks out of the holes in the knurled metal part of the grip better. Erasers are easy to find for it.

I use 3B (really soft) lead it as that's just what I like. When you see other people here say you can "adjust" the hardness with which it writes, don't be misled. The "adjustment" on the pencil is just a sticker underneath the hole in the grip so you can show what kind of lead you have loaded in your pencil. I think it ranges from 2B to 2H (I took the sticker off since I load it with 3B). But it is by no means a hardness adjustment. It's just an indicator. You still have to adjust hardness by switching out lead. If you were to have multiple Graphgear 1000 pencils then you could load them with different hardnesses and spin the indicator to the right setting so you know which lead you're writing with easily.

I use this as my daily writer for homework, labs, and sometimes notes. With the needle-like tip it's good for drawing diagrams, drafting, and the like.

t: Item not as good as I expected.
x: Pencil only had two small pieces of lead. Total length was one inch.  Did not work well and lead breaks easy.

Fantastic pencil! I take it everywhere I go! The grip is perfect and feels amazing in my hand the clip hiding the tip makes it perfect so that the lead doesn't just snap. There is an eraser hidden in the top where you insert the lead, it's tiny but can help on emergency mistakes. I would buy multiples of these just to have them but I really deeply feel like this is a pencil that will last forever! I suggest it to everyone!

t: It's a good pencil, but everything comes with some cons
x:
It's a good pencil, but everything comes with some cons:
- I have a tight grip and write hard. When doing so, the grip sometimes twists and unscrews itself. I think I got it to quit, but I had to tighten it so hard, it felt like I was going to break it.
- When you actuate the nib, the clip is what holds it out. When you push the clip, the pencil retracts really hard, and it feels like over time this will damage the plastic locking mechanism. I came up with a method where I keep the pencil actuated with my thumb, and release the clip gently.

All around decent pencil. I'm still anticipating finding my dream pencil, and sadly this wasn't it. If anyone has found a better pencil, let me know.

t: Not worth it or I just got a bad one

COMFORT: Note that this is a drafting pencil, which is why the nib is very long. That can be uncomfortable for extended writing periods. I never found this to be a problem, but I did notice it. The grip is excellent, and the pencil is well balanced.

So should you buy this? I wouldn't recommend this right away because I haven't seen the competition yet (Staedler?), but considering the fact that the inner barrel is plastic and the clip/retraction mechanism is so flimsy, I would rather go with the less complicated GG 500. That one has fewer moving parts, and thus harder to break. I would not buy this pencil again. This one's replacement will be the GG 500.

t: Really cool and stylish mechanical pencil

I was tired of going through cheap plastic mechanical pencils (if I could hold onto them long enough anyway), and wanted something durable and good-looking. The Pentel Graph Gear 1000 does just that. I bought one of these pencils at my university's bookstore expecting it to be the ultimate pencil (it is overpriced at over $20 here) and figured it would last me throughout the rest of my mathematical education; however, I was wrong.

The first couple of months, the pencil works like a dream. It has an amazing grip, great feel and weight, great features and function, and just an overall exterior feel of high quality. The problem lies beneath that high quality exterior and the true problems arise. The inner workings, in particular the division in the center of the pencil where the top half and the bottom half, with the grip, screw together are all made of brittle plastic. After two months of constant usage, the pencils failed when I tried to click for more lead and the center snapped sending the grip and lead tube through the outer shell and to my desk leaving the outer shell separated in my hand. The plastic piece was still screwed into the outer shell with no way of reversing or repairing the damage.

Essentially, the company went through all the processes of trying to make this pencil high quality, and tripped at the very end by making the pieces screw together via plastic rather than metal. This makes even the basic actions of clicking more lead a ticking time bomb to eventually cause the pencil to fail. This fatal flaw obviously makes this pencil essentially worthless, especially for the price.
